public_rationale: I read 'a pattern of slowing growth' as revenue growth decelerating in the latest results before the July 2024 post. Company releases show the opposite for most of the firms I could check. Microsoft's revenue grew 17% in the quarter to March 2024, up from 7% a year earlier. Meta's grew 27%, up from 3%. Apple is the exception: its revenue fell 4% in the same quarter, which fits his point for Apple alone. Overall, big tech growth was speeding up, not slowing, when he spoke. His second sentence, that there is no new thing to pick up and acquire, is a judgment about future growth engines. It cannot be measured, so it was not scored.
limitations: The company panel and the recent year-over-year baseline are my readings. He did not specify either.
Against the 2021 boom, growth was lower. A longer baseline could support his view.
Microsoft's growth includes the effect of the Activision acquisition.
Alphabet and Amazon are not among the cited items because their pages could not be read.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Big tech companies' growth is slowing, and they have no new thing to pick up or acquire to drive growth.

statement.excerpt: There is a pattern of slowing growth within these companies. And there isn't a new thing that they can pick up and acquire.
statement.document_title: Rot Economics - An Interview With MIT's Daron Acemoglu

from_speaker: a pattern of slowing growth within these companies
there isn't a new thing that they can pick up and acquire
our_interpretation: 'These companies' means the large tech firms discussed in the interview: Microsoft, Alphabet, Meta, Amazon, Apple and Nvidia. Nvidia is left out because he contrasts it with the rest.

Plain reading of 'pattern of slowing growth': the large tech firms' year-over-year revenue growth was decelerating as of mid-2024. The test compares the latest quarter reported before the post (mostly January to March 2024) with the same quarter a year earlier.
The target period runs from January 2023 to July 2024. It covers the latest reported quarters and their year-earlier comparisons. This is my choice for an ongoing-state claim and is flagged.
The second sentence ('there isn't a new thing that they can pick up and acquire') is a judgment about future growth engines with no measurable test. It is not scored. It is treated as context only.
criteria.support_condition: Most of these firms report lower year-over-year revenue growth in their latest pre-post quarter than in the year-earlier quarter, or a decline.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Most of these firms report faster year-over-year revenue growth in their latest pre-post quarter than a year earlier.

results for the quarter ended March 31, 2024, as compared to the corresponding period of last fiscal year:

· Revenue was $61.9 billion and increased 17%
evidence.explanation: Microsoft's revenue grew 17% in the quarter ended March 2024. Compared with 7% a year earlier (e2), that is acceleration, not slowing. Part of the growth came from the Activision acquisition.

evidence.explanation: This is the year-earlier baseline: 7% growth. Set against 17% in e1, it shows Microsoft's growth speeding up.
